text:
Maya: heads up — after importing the new hf/carrot-7b model the chat tests show shifted BOS/EOS ids, causing weird prefixing in replies.
Sam: ugh. repro on hosted or local import?
Maya: reproduced locally with our conversion script + quant pipeline. small repro: token ids for '<|bos|>' and '' moved by +2 vs the original vocab.
Jules: can you paste the `added_tokens.json` and `vocab.json` snippets? sometimes HF added_tokens ordering gets lost during our merge step.
Maya: sure — here's the relevant bits:
```json
// added_tokens.json
[ {"id": 50256, "special": true, "content": ""} ]
```
```json
// vocab.json (excerpt)
{"the": 0, "of": 1, "and": 2, "<|bos|>": 3}
```
Maya: but after conversion/token remap we see `<|bos|>` at id 5 and token 3 became a common token.
Sam: that smells like an index-shift when we concatenate added_tokens during hf->redwood merge. We have a step that reassigns ids: `merge_added_tokens(vocab, added_tokens)` — maybe the quantizer later prunes something and we don't rebase.
Jules: also check `tokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens(3)` before/after. If the embedding matrix rows don't match tokenizer ids you get garbage.
Maya: did that: before conversion `convert_ids_to_tokens(3) -> '<|bos|>'`, after conversion `convert_ids_to_tokens(3) -> ' the'`. Output sample:
```
Before: decode([3, 100, 101]) -> "<|bos|> Hello"
After:  decode([3, 100, 101]) -> " the Hello"
```
Sam: immediate mitigation — pin the special token ids in the tokenizer config to explicit numeric ids during import, e.g. `tokenizer._special_tokens_map = {'bos_token_id': 50256, 'eos_token_id': 50256}` then regenerate vocab mapping. Not ideal but buys time.
Maya: attempted that, but quantization step `quantize_model` trims unused embeddings based on `vocab_size` inference. If the tokenizer reports wrong `vocab_size` we lose rows.
Jules: steps I ran to debug: 1) `python -c "from transformers import AutoTokenizer; t=AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('hf/carrot-7b'); print(t.special_tokens_map, t.vocab_size)"` 2) open converted `vocab.bin` and assert shape matches `tokenizer.vocab_size` 3) run `python tools/check_id_alignment.py --model model.redwood --tokenizer tok.json` (added a small script that prints mismatches).
Maya: logs from check script: `MISMATCH id 3 token '<|bos|>' != 'the'` for 3 ids. Also found a pattern: id drift equals number of added_tokens present in hf/added_tokens.json that we failed to merge.
Sam: likely root cause: our merge logic assumed `added_tokens` had ids >= vocab_size, but HF sometimes uses absolute ids. When we reindex we offset incorrectly.
Jules: proposed fix: change merge to honor `id` field in added_tokens if present; only reassign if `id` is null. Add a validation: throw if any absolute id < current vocab_size and conflicts. Also add an invariant check in conversion pipeline that `convert_ids_to_tokens(tokenizer, embedding_matrix)` matches for a sample set.
Maya: +1. Also we should add an automated tiny eval: generate 50 tokens from seed prompt and compare token ids distribution vs upstream HF. If shift detected, fail the import.
infra-bot: deploy pipeline change MR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/merge-token-fix/pull/42 :eyes:
Sam: assign to @Jules?
Jules: assigning, I'll push a patch to conversion and add unit tests for three edge cases: (1) absolute ids in added_tokens, (2) empty added_tokens but nonzero `special_tokens_map`, (3) quant pruning when tokenizer reports stale `vocab_size`.
Maya: after local patch I re-ran quant import — BOS/EOS ids preserved and chat regression gone on our smoke prompts. Will run full eval overnight.
Sam: great. Please add a short note to the model-onboarding checklist: "verify id->token alignment post-conversion (use tools/check_id_alignment.py)".
Maya: creating ticket MODEL-1147 and linking sample artifacts (vocab diffs, check script output).
tokenizer-bot: note: archived original HF artifacts at s3://redwood-models/hf-carrot-7b/orig/1748654321/
Jules: thanks all — will post PR link when ready.
Maya: thanks — huge relief. :party_popper:
